text:
According to Natalie Harp's brother, his sister's devotion to the president stems from a need to replace her late father(Image: Getty Images)

White House aide Natalie Harp's brother is speaking out with assertions that her fixation with the president originates from a troubled relationship with her father.

Preston Harp claims that his estranged sister, whom he hasn't communicated with for many years, had maintained distance from her late father and had been searching for a substitute for years. "The way my sister interacted with and treated my dad throughout the years, it was like she wished she had a different dad," Preston told the Daily Beast.

The 38-year-old, who currently resides in Nicaragua, also suspects that his sister and the president have connected over American exceptionalism, an ideology that maintains that America is superior to other nations. Trump and Harp's purported belief aligns closely with his "America First" policy, which has removed several federal sites of their negative connections with U.S. history.

Preston stated about his sister: "While much of the media has focused on questioning whether her relationship is something scandalous, that is not where my mind goes personally. Maybe it is because I just can't imagine something like that, but to me this is 100 percent an infatuation based on an unfortunate shared ideology of U.S. exceptionalism."

"I think that she does see Trump as a kind of father figure because he embodies the doctrine of American exceptionalism," he added. Preston disclosed that, by comparison, his late father, who died by suicide in July 2020, did not "embody American exceptionalism in the least."

Natalie Harps' brother has revealed his sister's devotion to Donald Trump stems from issues she had with her father when she was younger(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

According to Preston, he had observed multiple holidays when his sister appeared to long for a different father. "Though I moved out at 18, I remember many Christmases, Easters, and Father's Day and Mother's Day get-togethers where I noticed this," said Preston.

Trump and Harp's relationship has allegedly triggered multiple concerns after the Secret Service identified her as a potential security risk. Reports indicate that Harp, who is frequently seen at the president's side, has been dubbed the "human printer" as the former conservative news anchor now dedicates her time to retrieving merchandise, conducting Google searches, printing news articles from conservative websites, and proposing Truth Social posts.

The aide has been seen glued to the president's side as he navigates his second term in office(Image: AP Photo/Mark Schiefelbein)

As the circle of individuals who maintain direct access to the president, 80, continues to shrink, Harp has become among the select few who endorsed Trump's Midas touch in the Oval Office.

New York Times White House correspondents Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan reported that Harp would frequently "gush with delight" over the new decor. "As the year progressed, he kept jamming more gold pieces onto the mantel," they wrote.

The devotion is so strong that the Secret Service has deemed Harp a possible security risk(Image: Getty Images)

"When Trump asked White House residence staff what they thought of the glittering display, most responses were muted, but his devout aide Natalie Harp would gush with delight," they added. The former White House reporters also discuss how Harp remained loyal to the president throughout his controversy-filled history.

The book also revealed that while Trump stayed secluded at his Mar-a-Lago estate, Harp was a regular presence on the golf course alongside the president. It was further claimed that she would leave the president multiple letters, including one that stated, "You are all that matters to me."

Harp was one of the few who applauded Trump's redecoration of the Oval Office(Image: AFP via Getty Images)

It was reported that the circumstances were so unusual that Susie Wiles, Trump's chief of staff, once supposedly questioned, "Where am I?" It was also noted that Trump started telling staff members during the initial months of his second term that "Nah-ta-lee," using the French pronunciation, "was the only one who loved him as much as his wife and his kids.

"All of you will go off and make money," he would tell his other staff members. "She'll never leave me."
